blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running audits and internal controls well means treating them as protection, not bureaucracy. Good controls catch real errors and real risks early, while they are still cheap to fix. A missed invoice, a duplicated payment, an expense approved by the wrong person — each of these is caught by a control that exists for a reason.

When an auditor arrives, the work should already be done. Every account has been reconciled, every document filed, every unusual entry documented. An audit that finds nothing is not a waste of time — it is the sign that the internal system has been quietly working.

Controls must be maintained, tested, and updated as the business changes. When they become boxes to tick instead of checks that actually protect, they quietly stop catching the things they were designed to catch — and the company only finds out long after the damage is done.

items.q: According to the text, how should audits and internal controls be treated?
items.why: "treating them as protection, not bureaucracy."

items.q: Why is catching an error early described as valuable?
options: Because it is still cheap to fix at that stage
Because it reduces the number of controls needed
Because it removes the need for documentation
items.why: "catch real errors and real risks early, while they are still cheap to fix."

items.q: What does the text say an audit that finds nothing actually means?
options: That the controls are no longer needed
That the auditor was not thorough
That the internal system has been quietly working
That the business has stopped growing
items.why: "it is the sign that the internal system has been quietly working."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Small errors are worth catching before they grow.
Controls that are never tested can fail silently.
Once a checklist is written, the controls can be left alone.
A clean audit can reflect good preparation.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que os controles precisam ser mantidos, testados e atualizados — nunca deixados intactos.

items.q: The final paragraph suggests that the real danger of a "box to tick" is that…
options: it is too expensive to maintain
it takes too long to complete
it fails without anyone noticing until later
items.why: Inferência: "they quietly stop catching… the company only finds out long after the damage is done."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicando como está reconstruindo os controles internos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, the audit last month flagged three problems, and honestly none of them should have got through. We had a checklist, it was signed every week, but nobody was actually checking anything — the boxes were just being ticked.

The first issue was a duplicated payment to a supplier. That should have been caught the moment two invoices with the same number came in. The second was an expense that was approved by the person who submitted it, which can never be allowed to happen again. And the third — a set of accounts that hadn't been reconciled for two quarters.

So here is what I'm changing. Every control now has to be tested, not just signed. Any payment over ten thousand must be approved by two people, and no one can approve their own expenses. Accounts will be reconciled monthly, and any unusual entry must be documented on the spot.

I'd rather the next audit finds nothing. If it does, it won't be luck — it'll mean the system is finally doing its job.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Charlotte say the old checklist failed?
options: It was too long to complete
It was signed by the wrong person
The boxes were ticked but nobody was actually checking
It had not been written down
items.why: "the boxes were just being ticked" — assinado sem checagem real.

items.q: What was wrong with the expense the audit found?
options: It was approved by the person who submitted it
items.why: "an expense that was approved by the person who submitted it".

items.q: What new rule does Charlotte introduce for larger payments?
options: They must be signed by the auditor
They must be approved by two people
They must be paid within ten days
items.why: "Any payment over ten thousand must be approved by two people".

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "I'd rather the next audit finds nothing"?
options: A clean audit would show the controls are working
She wants fewer controls in place
She expects the audit to be cancelled
She hopes the auditor does not come
items.why: Inferência: um relatório limpo seria a prova de que o sistema está protegendo de verdade.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's attitude?
options: Resigned and hoping for luck next time
Determined to make the controls genuinely work
items.why: Inferência: ela assume as falhas e impõe regras concretas — "it won't be luck".

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The team spends hours on paperwork that protects no one — pure bureaucracy." Bureaucracy here means…
options: procedure that adds effort without real value
items.why: Bureaucracy = burocracia: procedimento que gera esforço sem proteger de fato.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The control flagged a ___ payment — the same invoice had been settled twice."
items.why: Duplicated payment = pagamento em duplicidade: a mesma fatura paga duas vezes.

items.q: To reconcile an account means to…
options: check that two sets of records match
items.why: To reconcile = conciliar: conferir se dois registros batem entre si.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Any ___ entry — a number that looks out of place — must be documented straight away."
items.why: Unusual entry = lançamento incomum: um valor que parece fora do padrão.

items.q: "A good control will catch the error before it reaches the ledger." To catch here means to…
items.why: To catch = flagrar/detectar a tempo, antes que o erro avance.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas sobre auditoria e controles. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new control framework." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new approval rules across every desk." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on the two-signature rule." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de algo.

items.q: "They agreed to reconcile monthly but never followed through." They…
options: asked another team to do it
failed to carry it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A checklist that is signed without testing lets errors slip through the cracks." This means the errors…
items.why: Slip through the cracks = passar despercebido, escapar sem ser notado.
